description:
Second published-cutover fixture: `reviewPolicy: scope`. Uses the **4.2 harness** and a separate scenario file. Do not wait on the ticket-policy epic e2e.

## Background

Scope policy closes tickets from evidence then independently reviews the **aggregate** before declaring the epic complete. Dependents may start before aggregate review finds a problem. Prove that tradeoff. Do not mix policies in one script.

Do **not** build an immutable review-subject protocol, OID manifests, or dependency graphs. Reviewer prompts target **named commits / ticket ids** (`git show`), same as shared-checkout guidance.

## Scenario

1. Epic with two tickets, policy scope.
2. `/bw run`, implement both, parent accepts/closes from evidence **without** per-ticket `reviewImplementation` children.
3. Dependent may start after parent close (not after settle).
4. One `reviewScope` child against the aggregate (named commits/tickets), not ambient workspace-only.
5. Blocking finding → in-scope remediation + re-review as scripted parent turns.
6. Epic close only after scope-review dispositions are done.
7. Logs: policy=scope, ticket ids, proof that **zero** ticket-review children were launched, scope-review child id, dispositions.

## Success criteria

- No per-ticket `reviewImplementation` children under scope policy.
- Ticket-policy fixture (sibling) still requires them.
- tmux absent. Scripted parent, no paid LLM. No worktree.

## Test plan

- Dedicated scenario file on the 4.2 harness.
- Failure dumps last packet, `bw show` epic, child taskTypes launched.

## Considerations

Does not need peer/mail (`3.x`). Blocked by harness (4.2), review goldens (4.1), goal-exit (2.6), and runtime deletion (2.7).

comments.text: Do not mix ticket and scope policy in one fixture. Share the scripted-parent harness from the ticket-policy epic e2e.

title: Prove scope-policy epic fixture without per-ticket review children
